title: Air Traffic Procedures
description: Key concepts from AIM Chapter 5 covering preflight planning, flight plans, NOTAMs, departure/arrival procedures, and instrument approaches

cards.back:
Before flight, become familiar with ALL available information:
• Weather reports and forecasts
• Fuel requirements
• Alternatives if flight cannot be completed
• Known ATC traffic delays
• Runway lengths at airports of intended use
• Takeoff and landing distance data

STANDARD: Complete briefing for planning
• Request when no prior briefing received

ABBREVIATED: Update/supplement to prior briefing
• Request specific information only

OUTLOOK: For planning purposes
• Departure 6+ hours away
• General weather trends

NOTAM (D): Disseminated to all pilots
• Aeronautical facilities, services, procedures
• Navigational aids, obstacles

FDC NOTAM: Flight Data Center
• Regulatory - amendments to procedures
• TFRs and airspace changes

Military NOTAMs
• Affects military operations

• NOT required but RECOMMENDED
• Provides search and rescue protection
• File via phone, internet, or app
• ACTIVATE before departure
• CLOSE upon arrival (or SAR initiates!)
• Valid for 2 hours after proposed departure
• Does NOT provide ATC services

C - Clearance limit (usually destination)
R - Route of flight
A - Altitude (initial and expect)
F - Frequency (departure control)
T - Transponder code

Always READ BACK complete clearance!

Fly in this order (AVE-F):

A - Assigned (last route assigned by ATC)
V - Vectored (direct to fix, route, or airway being vectored to)
E - Expected (route ATC said to expect)
F - Filed (route in flight plan)

Maintain the HIGHEST of:

• Last ASSIGNED altitude
• Altitude ATC said to EXPECT
• MINIMUM en route altitude (MEA)

Remember: 'Highest of the three'

Also squawk 7600!

• Preplanned IFR departure procedure
• Provides obstacle clearance
• Improves traffic flow
• Simplifies clearance delivery

Types:
• Pilot Nav - pilot navigates the route
• Vector - ATC vectors after takeoff
• Must have charts to accept SID

• Preplanned IFR arrival procedure
• Transition from en route to terminal
• Simplifies clearance delivery
• Reduces pilot/controller workload
• May include altitude/speed restrictions
• Must have chart to accept STAR

DIRECT (within 70° sector):
• Turn right, fly pattern

TEARDROP (from 70° opposite side):
• Fly outbound 30° offset, turn to inbound

PARALLEL (from remaining sector):
• Fly outbound parallel, turn back to fix

'When in doubt, go direct'

Below 6,000' MSL: 200 KIAS
6,001' - 14,000' MSL: 230 KIAS
Above 14,000' MSL: 265 KIAS

Leg timing (below 14,000'):
• Inbound leg: 1 minute
• Above 14,000': 1.5 minutes

OR: DME/GPS distance if specified

• Provided when entering holding
• Time to expect clearance to continue
• CRITICAL for lost comm procedures

If lost comm while holding:
• Leave holding fix at EFC time
• Continue via expected route
• Begin approach at expected time

DA (Decision Altitude):
• Precision approaches (ILS, GLS)
• Continue descent if visual
• Initiate missed if not

MDA (Minimum Descent Altitude):
• Non-precision approaches
• Level off at MDA
• Only descend when runway in sight
• May not descend below without visual ref

Must see at least ONE:
• Approach light system (if can identify threshold)
• Threshold or markings
• Threshold lights
• REIL (Runway End Identifier Lights)
• VASI/PAPI
• Touchdown zone or markings
• Touchdown zone lights
• Runway or markings
• Runway lights

• Course reversal to establish inbound
• Normally within 10 NM of fix
• Remain on maneuvering side
• NOT authorized when:
 - 'NoPT' shown
 - Radar vectors to final
 - Timed approach
 - Holding in lieu of PT
• Barbed arrow shows direction

• Defined point on non-precision approach
• Normal 3° descent from MDA to runway
• Shown as 'V' on approach plate
• If no VDP, may need steeper descent
• Helps with stabilized approach
• Not required to use, but recommended

Non-Precision:
• Maltese cross symbol on profile
• Begin descent, start timing

Precision:
• Lightning bolt (glideslope intercept)
• Where glidepath is intercepted

Always at published altitude when crossing FAF

• Visual maneuver to land on different runway
• Higher minimums than straight-in
• Protected areas by aircraft category:
 - Cat A: 1.3 NM
 - Cat B: 1.5 NM
 - Cat C: 1.7 NM
 - Cat D: 2.3 NM
• Remain at MDA until in position to land
• If lost visual, execute missed

Upon going missed:
1. Apply full power, climb
2. Follow published procedure
3. Advise ATC as soon as practical

Procedure includes:
• Initial climb instructions
• Turning instructions
• Holding fix and altitude

Don't delay - act immediately!

• Assigned by ATC (or requested)
• Requires: ceiling ≥1,000', visibility ≥3 SM
• Pilot must have airport OR preceding aircraft in sight
• IFR flight plan remains active
• Pilot responsible for obstruction clearance
• Can be assigned even without approach procedure

• Must be REQUESTED by pilot (never assigned)
• Requires: 1 SM flight visibility, clear of clouds
• Pilot must reasonably expect to continue
• Airport must have an IAP
• Pilot responsible for obstruction clearance
• Lower requirements than visual approach

Based on approach speed (Vref x 1.3):

A: <91 knots
B: 91-120 knots
C: 121-140 knots
D: 141-165 knots
E: >165 knots

Use higher category if circling faster than normal approach speed

May cancel:
• Anytime in VFR conditions
• Except Class A (IFR required)

Benefits:
• Releases airspace for others
• No approach sequence delay
• More flexibility

Caution:
• No IFR separation once cancelled
• Can't reenter clouds
• May need new clearance if weather deteriorates

ODP (Obstacle Departure Procedure):
• Provides obstacle clearance only
• Textual or graphical
• Not assigned by ATC
• Pilot's responsibility to use

SID:
• ATC procedure for traffic flow
• Must be assigned/accepted
• Also provides obstacle clearance

Part 91 (not required to comply, but recommended):

1 & 2 engine: 1 SM visibility
3+ engines: 1/2 SM visibility

Non-standard minimums:
• Symbol 'T' in approach chart margin
• Check departure procedure
• May require higher minimums or climb gradient

Localizer: Lateral guidance (27.9 NM)
• 'Blue/Yellow' or 'Fly Left/Right'

Glide Slope: Vertical guidance
• Usually 3° angle
• 10 NM range

Marker Beacons:
• OM (Outer): Blue, dashes
• MM (Middle): Amber, dots/dashes
• IM (Inner): White, dots

Approach Lights: Visual transition

LNAV: Lateral navigation only (non-precision)
LP: Localizer Performance (WAAS, no vertical)
LNAV/VNAV: Lateral + vertical nav (baro-VNAV)
LPV: Localizer Performance with Vertical (WAAS)

LPV provides near-ILS precision with WAAS GPS

• Authorizes flight at any altitude from minimum IFR to assigned
• May climb/descend at pilot's discretion
• Once leaving altitude, may NOT return to it without clearance
• Includes clearance for approach at destination
• Report leaving each altitude

• Fly VFR altitudes (odd+500 E, even+500 W)
• Must maintain VFR cloud clearance
• Still on IFR flight plan
• ATC separation still provided
• Must request - 'Request VFR-on-top'
• Cannot be assigned by ATC
• Not available in Class A

Purpose: Visual transition from instruments

Types:
• ALSF-1, ALSF-2: With sequenced flashers
• MALSR: Medium intensity
• MALSF: With flashers
• SSALR, SSALF: Simplified short
• ODALS: Omnidirectional

With ALS, can descend to 100' above TDZE if see ALS and can identify threshold

On CTAF frequency:
7 clicks: High intensity
5 clicks: Medium intensity
3 clicks: Low intensity

• Within 5 seconds
• Lights stay on ~15 minutes
• Works for runway, approach, VASI/PAPI
• Key again to change intensity or reset timer

Declare when:
• Cannot accept undue delay
• Emergency fuel status NOT YET reached

Phrase: 'Minimum Fuel'

NOT an emergency declaration
Informs ATC of priority need

If fuel critical:
Declare EMERGENCY instead

RAIM: Receiver Autonomous Integrity Monitoring

Required:
• Verify RAIM availability preflight
• Check GPS NOTAMs
• Must be present for approach

If RAIM fails during approach:
• Cannot continue to DA/MDA
• Execute missed approach
• Report to ATC

• Shown on approach charts
• 1,000 feet obstacle clearance
• Within 25 NM of facility/waypoint
• For emergency use only
• Does NOT guarantee NAVAID reception
• May be divided into sectors

Report at each compulsory reporting point:
1. Aircraft identification
2. Position
3. Time (UTC)
4. Altitude/FL
5. Type of flight plan
6. ETA next reporting point
7. Name of following point
8. Remarks

Solid triangle = compulsory
Open triangle = on request
